content.title: Urban Governance In Non-Equilibrium Society: Maintenance, Transformation, And Public Capacity
content.abstract: Urban governance acts within processes sustained by material throughput, maintenance, movement, interpretation and institutional authority. Stable outputs can conceal declining support, while structural change can preserve or expand a public function. This paper develops a mechanism-centered inquiry into these possibilities. It presents all 53 classes of a five-level non-equilibrium taxonomy and examines each through urban phenomena, practical problems, ontological commitments, epistemic limits and methods of intervention.
